intended_object: The canonical isomorphism K₀(R) ≅ ℤ for a local ring R, which may be noncommutative. It sends the class of a finitely generated projective module P to the dimension of P ⊗_R R/J(R) over the residue division ring R/J(R) (Weibel, *The K-book*, II §2). This is inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition is `AddEquiv.ofBijective` applied to `localDimensionHom R`. That map first pushes classes in K₀ forward along the quotient map R → R/J(R). Because R is local, the Jacobson radical J(R) is maximal, so the quotient is a division ring. The map then takes the dimension over that division ring (`finrankHom`). This matches the textbook construction exactly.

Bijectivity is a proved lemma (`localDimensionHom_bijective`). The library also proves that the equivalence sends [R] to 1 and that its inverse sends an integer n to n·[R], which is the standard behaviour.

The setting is the right one. Mathlib's `IsLocalRing` on a noncommutative `Ring` is the usual notion of a noncommutative local ring, and the statement is about local rings themselves, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no K₀ and no such equivalence, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
